_doc: Fated turning points. The situation is certain; outcome = 70% chart (destinyScript chartWeights) + 30% the chosen strategy (choice weights). Among variants whose 'requires' hold (and whose speaker can speak), the highest 'priority' wins; ties are picked at random per event. 'compat' lets 궁합 with the destined person bend outcomes (+1 grows, −1 shrinks) when they are involved; 'withFated' puts them in the scene; 'title' heads the big popup. 'card' shows in the 시간이 흐른다 screen; 'scene' moves the player for the rest of the day.

hint.ko: (요즘 이상하게 누군가를 만날 것 같은 예감이 든다.)
hint.en: (Lately you have a strange feeling you're about to meet someone.)

line.ko: (자꾸 눈이 마주치던 그 사람이 먼저 다가왔다.)
line.en: (The person whose eyes kept meeting yours walks over.)

r.ko: 그날 밤, 한참을 이야기했다. 이상하게 오래 알던 사람 같았다. 그날부터 연락이 끊이지 않았다.
r.en: You talked for hours that night. It felt like you'd known them forever. After that, the texts never stopped.
You started texting now and then.

r.ko: …그 사람은 인파 속으로 사라졌다. 계속 생각이 난다.
r.en: …They disappeared into the crowd. You keep thinking about them.

effects.text: A missed connection I still remember.

line.ko: (연인이 있는데도, 이상하게 마음이 흔들리는 사람을 만났다.)
line.en: (Even though you're with someone, you meet a person who shakes you.)

r.ko: …결국 지금의 연인과 헤어졌다. 자꾸만 그 사람에게 마음이 갔다.
r.en: …In the end you broke up. Your heart kept drifting to them.

r.ko: 좋은 친구로 남았다. 가끔 생각이 난다.
r.en: You stayed good friends. Sometimes you wonder.
You never contacted them again.

line.ko: (오늘따라 {fated}에게서 눈을 뗄 수가 없다. 이 마음, 전해볼까?)
line.en: (Today you can't take your eyes off {fated}. Should you tell them how you feel?)

r.ko: (심장이 터질 것 같다. 오늘, 말하기로 했다.)
r.en: (Your heart is pounding. Today, you're going to say it.)
You're growing closer, little by little. Friends, for now.
…{fated} already had someone in their heart.

line.ko: (친구가 소개해 준 사람과 저녁을 먹었다. 이야기가 끝없이 이어졌다.)
line.en: (Dinner with someone a friend introduced. The conversation just kept going.)

r.ko: 그날 밤, 한참을 이야기했다. 오래 알던 사람 같았다.
r.en: You talked late into the night. It felt like you'd known each other for years.
You started texting now and then.
A good person, but not the one.

line.ko: (…{partner}와(과) 함께 걷는 길. 이상하게, 처음부터 알던 사람 같다.)
line.en: (…Walking with {partner}. Strangely, it feels like you've always known each other.)

r.en: That day you were sure: it's this person.
You're not sure yet. But it's good.
…Lately you feel a little distant.

line.ko: (요즘 {partner}와(과) 보내는 시간이 부쩍 늘었다.)
line.en: (You've been spending more and more time with {partner}.)

r.en: You grew closer.
Quiet, ordinary days went on.
…Things feel a little stale lately.

hint.en: (You've been thinking a lot about the future lately.)

line.ko: …있잖아. 우리, 결혼할까?
line.en: …Hey. Should we get married?

t.en: Let me think a little more
…I think this is where we end

r.en: You got the ring. Your hands were shaking.
…Okay, I'll wait. But how long?
That day, we broke up.

line.ko: (결혼 준비로 정신이 없다. {partner}이(가) 청첩장 시안 두 개를 내밀었다.) 이거랑 이거, 뭐가 나아?
line.en: (Wedding prep is chaos. {partner} holds out two invitation drafts.) This one or this one?

r.ko: 우리 이름이 나란히 적힌 청첩장. 그제야 실감이 났다.
r.en: Your two names side by side on the invitation. Only then did it feel real.

r.ko: 결혼 준비로 처음 크게 다퉜다. 그래도 식은 예정대로 하기로 했다.
r.en: Your first big fight — over the wedding. The date stays, though.
…The invitations were never printed.

line.ko: (예전에 알던 그 사람을 다시 만났다. 둘 다 혼자였다.)
line.en: (You run into someone from before. You're both single.)

t.en: Don't let them go this time

r.ko: 다시 연락하기 시작했다. 이번엔 다를 것 같다.
r.en: You started talking again. It feels different this time.
You meet for coffee now and then.
You decided to keep it a good memory.

line.ko: 우리 결혼기념일인데… 앞으로도 잘 부탁해.
line.en: It's our anniversary… let's keep taking care of each other.

r.en: You walked hand in hand for the first time in a while.
A quiet evening.
…The conversation kept missing.

line.ko: (소개팅 자리. 마주 앉은 사람이 먼저 웃었다.)
line.en: (A blind date. The person across the table smiled first.)

r.ko: 연락이 이어졌다. 어느새 매일 밤 통화를 하고 있었다.
r.en: The texts kept coming. Soon you were calling every night.
You agreed to meet a few more times.
A good person, but not the one.

line.ko: 우리… 이대로 괜찮은 걸까?
line.en: Are we… really okay like this?

r.en: After tears and laughter, you held each other.

effects.text: We got through a hard night together.

r.en: …It was over.
You agreed to keep some distance for a while.

line.ko: (헤어진 사람에게서 연락이 왔다. "잘 지내?")
line.en: (A message from an ex: "How have you been?")

r.en: You met after a long time. They had changed.
You left the past in the past.
You just said hi.

line.ko: ({partner}의 휴대폰에 낯선 이름의 메시지가 떴다. …그리고 오늘, 둘이 함께 있는 걸 봤다.)
line.en: (A message from an unfamiliar name lit up {partner}'s phone. …And today, you saw them together.)

r.ko: {partner}이(가) 무릎을 꿇었다. …딱 한 번만, 믿어보기로 했다.
r.en: {partner} fell to their knees. …You decided to trust them, just once more.
…You couldn't stay together anymore.

r.ko: 아무 말도 하지 못했다. 그날 이후, 우리 사이엔 금이 갔다.
r.en: You couldn't say a word. Since that day, something between you cracked.

line.ko: 잠깐 얘기 좀 할까요? 회사에 큰 변화가 있을 거예요.
line.en: Got a minute? Big changes are coming to the company.

r.en: Promoted to team lead! The team applauded.

r.ko: …구조조정 명단에 이름이 있었다. 상자에 짐을 쌌다.
r.en: …Your name was on the restructuring list. You packed a box.
You resigned and started your own thing.

line.ko: 면접 결과를 알려드리려고 연락드렸어요.
line.en: We're calling about your interview.

t.en: Actually, I want to do my own thing

r.en: You're hired! Start next week.
…Unfortunately, it won't work out this time.
You opened a small shop.

hint.en: (Lately you strangely want to go somewhere far…)

line.ko: (역마가 또 들썩인다. 여기서 산 지도 꽤 됐다. 문득 {homeland} 생각이 난다.)
line.en: (The travelling star stirs again. You've lived here a while now. {homeland} crosses your mind.)

r.ko: 몇 년 만의 인천공항. 공기 냄새부터 달랐다. 돌아왔다.
r.en: Incheon Airport after all these years. Even the air smelled different. You were home.

r.ko: 같은 나라, 새 도시. 짐 싸는 건 이제 익숙하다.
r.en: Same country, new city. You're used to packing by now.

r.ko: 여기가 이제 내 동네다. 단골 가게 사장님이 이름을 불러줬다.
r.en: This is your neighborhood now. The owner of your usual place called you by name.

line.ko: (멀리 떠날 수 있는 기회가 생겼다. 해외 근무, 유학, 새 도시…)
line.en: (A chance to go far: work abroad, study, a new city…)

r.ko: 비행기 창밖으로 구름이 보였다. 새로운 시작이다.
r.en: Clouds outside the plane window. A new beginning.
You loaded the moving truck.

r.ko: 익숙한 동네에 남기로 했다. 대신 여행을 떠났다.
r.en: You stayed in the familiar neighborhood, but took a trip instead.

line.ko: [아빠] 엄마가 입원했다. 올 수 있니?
line.en: [Dad] Mom's in the hospital. Can you come?

r.ko: …의사가 가족들을 불렀다. 오늘 밤을 넘기기 어렵다고 했다.
r.en: …The doctor called the family in. Tonight may be the last.

r.ko: 엄마가 회복했다. 퇴원하던 날 같이 웃었다.
r.en: Mom recovered. You laughed together the day she left the hospital.

line.ko: 아빠가 쓰러지셨어. 빨리 와.
line.en: Dad collapsed. Come quickly.

r.ko: …의사가 고개를 저었다. 아빠 곁에 있어 드리라고 했다.
r.en: …The doctor shook his head. 'Stay with your dad.'
Dad got back on his feet.

line.ko: ({relative}께서 돌아가셨다는 연락을 받았다.)
line.en: (You got word that {relative} passed away.)

t.en: (You sit there, numb, for a long time)

r.ko: 오랜만에 모인 친척들과 옛날 이야기를 했다.
r.en: You shared old stories with relatives you hadn't seen in years.

line.ko: [이모] 엄마가 입원하셨어. 올 수 있겠니?
line.en: [Aunt] Your mom's in the hospital. Can you come?

r.ko: …의사가 가족들을 불렀다. 오늘 밤을 넘기기 어렵다고 했다.
r.en: …The doctor called the family in. Tonight may be the last.

r.ko: 엄마가 회복했다. 퇴원하던 날 같이 웃었다.
r.en: Mom recovered. You laughed together the day she left the hospital.

line.ko: 이번에 큰 기회가 있는데, 같이 해볼래?
line.en: There's a big opportunity—want in?

r.ko: 대박이 났다! 통장 잔고를 몇 번이나 확인했다.
r.en: It paid off big! You checked your balance again and again.
…You lost it all. You couldn't sleep for a while.
Nothing much happened. That was a relief.

line.ko: (오래 지켜본 투자처가 있다. 지금이 기회일지도 모른다.)
line.en: (There's an investment you've been watching for ages. Maybe now's the time.)

r.ko: 대박이 났다! 통장 잔고를 몇 번이나 확인했다.
r.en: It paid off big! You checked your balance again and again.
…You lost it all. You couldn't sleep for a while.
Nothing much happened. That was a relief.

line.ko: …나 할 말이 있어. 우리, 아기가 생겼어.
line.en: …I have something to tell you. We're having a baby.

r.en: You held each other for a long time.
…Not this time. You were both quiet.

line.ko: 우리 나중에 아이 낳으면 어떨까?
line.en: What would it be like if we had kids someday?

r.en: Marriage feels a little closer.
For now, the two of you is enough.

hint.ko: (퇴근길에 자꾸 유기동물 보호소 앞을 지나게 된다.)
hint.en: (You keep passing the animal shelter on your way home.)

line.ko: 보호소에서 입양 행사 중이에요. 한번 보고 가실래요?
line.en: There's an adoption event at the shelter. Want to take a look?

r.ko: 집에 온 첫날, 강아지가 내 발 위에서 잠들었다.
r.en: The first night home, the puppy fell asleep on your feet.

r.ko: 고양이가 소파 밑에서 나오지 않는다. 그래도 좋다.
r.en: The cat won't come out from under the sofa. Still, it's nice.
You signed up to volunteer instead.

hint.en: (Talk of early-retirement packages is going around at work.)

line.ko: 이번에 명예퇴직 신청을 받는데… 한번 생각해 보시겠어요?
line.en: We're taking early-retirement applications… would you consider it?

r.ko: 명예퇴직금을 받고 회사를 떠났다. 마지막 날, 꽃다발을 받았다.
r.en: You left with an early-retirement package. On the last day, they gave you flowers.
You decided to stay until retirement age.
After leaving, you started something new.

line.ko: (앞으로 남은 인생을 어떻게 보낼지 생각해 본다.)
line.en: (You think about how to spend the rest of your life.)

r.en: Easygoing days began.
Days passed quietly.
You started learning something new.

line.ko: (가게를 계속할까, 이제 내려놓을까. 셔터를 내리며 생각한다.)
line.en: (Keep the shop going, or let it go? You wonder as you pull down the shutter.)

r.ko: 마지막 손님을 배웅하고 가게 문을 닫았다. 단골들이 꽃을 두고 갔다.
r.en: You saw off the last customer and closed the shop. Regulars left flowers.
You decided to open the shutter again tomorrow.

r.ko: 가게를 넘기고, 전혀 다른 일을 배우기 시작했다.
r.en: You handed over the shop and started learning something totally different.

hint.ko: (요즘 따라 가족들 건강이 자꾸 신경 쓰인다.)
hint.en: (Lately you keep worrying about everyone's health.)

line.ko: {patient}의 검사 결과… 암이 발견됐습니다.
line.en: {patient}'s results… we found cancer.

r.ko: 힘든 싸움이 시작됐다. 그래도 희망이 있다.
r.en: A hard fight begins. But there is hope.
They said it would be a long treatment.
…It was further along than anyone thought.
